isolationIncident.cause: The test imported the broadcast singleton before changing cwd; its eager settings dependency fixed the Node-only fallback directory at the project root.
isolationIncident.observedContent: 10000 generated test tags and a library path within .tmp/refactor-tests/settings-feed-RNKrwv; synthetic privacy setup from the verifier.
isolationIncident.scope: Project Node fallback settings file. The ordinary Electron runtime uses app.getPath('userData'); no writes to that path were issued by this verifier.
isolationIncident.priorFileContent: Not captured before the unintended test write; no reliable original backup was found in the fallback directory.
isolationIncident.action: Kept the file in place. Changed broadcast repository loading to lazy initialization and added an explicit per-fixture user-data path assertion before any test write.
isolationIncident.rerun: Passed with user data rooted inside .tmp/refactor-tests/settings-feed-Q02dcP. No speculative restoration or deletion performed.
isolationIncident.guards: Broadcast repository is lazy. Node verifier asserts fixture user data before any setting write. Native verifier sets and asserts Electron userData. UI/cost wrappers compare project fallback hash before and after. Successful corrected regressions and the three final cost pairs retained the documented project fallback content.

limits: Initial/full recovery/legacy event and desktop mutation reply paths can still copy full settings; no new public HTTP payload or mobile capability is required.
Top-level arrays remain complete fields; map reordering may carry the full key order. Huge single-entity data is not a narrow payload guarantee.
Main callback clone, normalization, event map scan, postMessage clone and selected-field serialization still cost CPU/memory; tag total time did not improve.
Compatibility sync paths and rebases intentionally fall back to full snapshots. Legacy listeners keep their old complete snapshot contract.
The Node model and isolated Electron feed test have different path/key lengths and cannot be compared as native before/after latency.
No original fallback-settings content was captured before the accidental test overwrite. File retained, no speculative restore or delete.
R6 physical decode/contention/rotation/PSS, R7 remaining full read/type/feature/cold-start work, R8 dependency/migration/recovery/signing/update/TLS remain open.
